back: An industry sited near its raw materials because they are heavy, bulky, perishable or lose weight in processing (e.g. sugar milling).
An industry sited near its customers because the product gains weight, is bulky, fragile or perishable (e.g. bottling, baking).
An industry not tied to raw materials or markets, free to locate in many places (e.g. electronics, software).
The clustering of related industries so they share suppliers, services, skilled labour and infrastructure.
An industry staying in its original location after the first location factors have gone.
Moving goods in standard steel containers that transfer easily between ship, rail and lorry, cutting transport costs.
Raw materials, power, water and land (site).
Labour, capital, markets, transport, government policy, technology and communications, agglomeration.
Triangle and Hippo Valley in the south-east Lowveld: next to irrigated cane estates, as cane is heavy and perishable.
